verses.text: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, appointed to strengthen the faith of God's chosen people and help them know the truth that leads to godliness,
and to give them hope of eternal life. God, who never lies, promised that life before time began.
At the right time, he revealed his message through the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior.
To Titus, my true child in our shared faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
I left you in Crete for this reason: to set right what was unfinished and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.
An elder must be above reproach, faithful to one wife, and have children who believe and aren't known for wild or rebellious behavior.
An overseer, as God's steward, must be above reproach. They must not be arrogant, quick-tempered, addicted to wine, violent, or greedy for dishonest gain.
Instead, they should welcome guests, love what is good, be sensible, fair, holy, and self-controlled.
They must hold firmly to the trustworthy message as it was taught, so they can encourage others with sound teaching and correct those who oppose it.
There are many rebellious people, empty talkers, and deceivers, especially among those who insist on circumcision.
They must be silenced, because they are upsetting whole households by teaching what they shouldn't for dishonest profit.
One of their own prophets said, ‘Cretans are always liars, vicious beasts, and lazy gluttons.’
That statement is true. So correct them sharply, so they may become sound in the faith
and stop paying attention to Jewish myths and commands from people who turn away from the truth.
To the pure, everything is pure. But to those who are corrupted and don't believe, nothing is pure; both their minds and consciences are corrupted.
They claim to know God, but their actions deny him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
